newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - No jobs in Canberra labour reforms - Democrat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - No jobs in Canberra labour reforms - Democrat.

text.p: Australian Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot said on Wednesday the government's proposed industrial relations changes would not reduce unemployment.
"You (the government) said unemployment was your number one election priority and you're not delivering on it," Kernot told Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio.
Official data released last week showed the jobless rate increased to 8.8 percent in August from 8.5 percent in July.
"I think one of the key points of the Workplace Relations Bill is to give flexibility to those who already have jobs at the high end of the market," Kernot said.
"What have we got from this government, we've got no long term solution for unemployment," she said.

Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone has urged the Labor opposition and the minor parties, including the Democrats, which hold the balance of power in the upper house of parliament, the Senate, not to block the government's labour market reforms, embodied in its Workplace Relations Bill.

Kernot said: "What we're saying is it's our (the Democrats) responsibility to make sure that, as we move in this evolutionary fashion, we don't let them go too far, too soon, and we put in place appropriate safeguards, particularly for the bottom third of the workforce who will not benefit from the flexibility of a deregulated labour market."
The Democrats have been negotiating with the government over amendments to the Workplace Relations Bill.
"We've said we'll look at it, but we say don't say this is going to deliver the magic solution to unemployment," Kernot said.
"Your (the government's) budget is built on the back of unemployed people in this country," she said.
"I'm not saying the Workplace Relations Bill will have a net negative effect."

"I'm just saying it's dishonest to claim that the solutions to our unemployment, in the longer term and in the short term, are two magical things - pass the budget and let us have our Workplace Relations Bill."

She said the solutions to unemployment would come from infrastructure spending, taxation reform, access to finance, better access to finance for small business and more money spent on research and development.
The government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate. The seven-strong Australian Democrats are its only likely source of votes to get the Workplace Relations Bill passed.
